summary.text: The heart is a muscular organ that pumps blood through the blood vessels, and together they make up the circulatory system.
The pumped blood carries oxygen and nutrients to the tissues and carries metabolic waste such as carbon dioxide to the lungs.
In humans the heart has four chambers, two upper atria and two lower ventricles, and valves make sure blood flows only one way through it.

facts.label: Resting rate
facts.value: Close to 72 beats per minute in adults

facts.label: Location
facts.value: Between the lungs, in the chest's mediastinum

facts.label: Rhythm setter
facts.value: Pacemaker cells in the sinoatrial node

items.prompt: Between beats, blood in a healthy heart keeps moving forward instead of flowing backward. What makes this possible?

options.label: The cardiac notch in the lung

items.explain: In a healthy heart, blood flows one way because heart valves prevent backflow.

items.prompt: Which cells decide the rhythm at which the heart contracts?

options.label: Collagen of the cardiac skeleton tissue
Cells of the protective sac, the pericardium
Cells of the heart wall's outer epicardium
Pacemaker cells of the sinoatrial node

items.explain: A group of pacemaker cells in the sinoatrial node sets the rhythm by generating an electric current that makes the heart contract.

items.prompt: Picture the heart's upper chambers as an entry hall where blood is received. What are those chambers called?
items.explain: The two upper chambers, the atria, are the receiving chambers; the lower ventricles are the discharging chambers.

items.prompt: Oxygen-poor blood comes back from the body through the venae cavae. Which chamber does it enter first?
items.explain: Deoxygenated blood from the venae cavae enters the right atrium and passes to the right ventricle.

items.prompt: The left side of the heart is stronger and larger than the right. Why?

options.label: It pumps blood only to the lungs
It sits closer to the vertebral column
It pumps blood to all parts of the body

items.explain: The left heart is stronger and larger because it pumps to all body parts.

items.prompt: A well-trained athlete's heart is much larger than average. What explains this?

options.label: Exercise builds the heart muscle, much like skeletal muscle
Athletes are born with extra chambers
Their heart sits lower in the chest

items.explain: Exercise affects the heart muscle in a way similar to the response of skeletal muscle, so well-trained athletes can have much larger hearts.
